story.head: Panarin’s favorite opponent
paras: The Kings (4-6-2) beat Ottawa 6-5 in overtime on Thursday, and the Sabres have won two in a row. Going in, the Sabres are seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Kings seventh in the Pacific (tied for 28th).

The Sabres’ record (.577) is about what their chances are worth. The Kings have played better than their record (.417) says: their chances are worth about .573, and their finishing has held them back. If the Kings’ record were closer to their chances, like the Sabres’, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Sabres get their shots through better than almost anyone (2nd) and rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd), but don't block many shots (30th). On the other side, the Kings take away shots from the point (4th lowest) and take a lot of low-quality shots (31st). They also leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest), so the Sabres’ defensemen shoot a lot, and theirs not so much. The Sabres’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Kings.

Tage Thompson (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 13 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Jack Quinn (7 G / 5 A / 12 P in 13 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 5 A / 13 P in 12 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in nine straight games against Buffalo.
Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (3-3-3 / .866 SV% in 8 GS) has struggled for Buffalo so far, but is expected to start. Darcy Kuemper (4-3-1 / .878 SV% in 8 GS) is expected to go for Los Angeles.

items.text: The Sabres are newly without Konsta Helenius, have been without Jiří Kulich since Oct 21, and have had to make do without Alex Lyon and Conor Timmins all season. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is expected to start.
The Kings are newly without Mats Zuccarello, have been without Alex Turcotte since Oct 6, and have had to make do without Kevin Fiala all season.
Adrian Kempe has three goals on chances worth about 6.5 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Tage Thompson is two goals from passing René Robert for ninth on the Sabres’ all-time goals list.
